arxiv-2007-10958.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by David Kozhaya 1 , Jérémie Decouchant 2,∗ , Vincent Rahli 3,† , and Paulo Esteves-Verissimo 4,∗. The accelerated digitalisation of society along with technological evolution have extended the geographical span of cyber-physical systems. Two main threats have made the reliable and real-time control of these systems challenging: (i) uncertainty in the communication infrastructure induced by scale, and heterogeneity of the environment and devices; and (ii) targeted attacks maliciously worsening the impact of the above-mentioned communication uncertainties, disrupting the correctness of real-time applications.

arxiv-2105-09371.title: VOILA: Visual-Observation-Only Imitation Learning for Autonomous Navigation
arxiv-2105-09371.creator: Haresh Karnan, Garrett Warnell, Xuesu Xiao, Peter Stone
arxiv-2105-09371.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Haresh Karnan, Garrett Warnell, Xuesu Xiao, Peter Stone. While imitation learning for vision-based autonomous mobile robot navigation has recently received a great deal of attention in the research community, existing approaches typically require state-action demonstrations that were gathered using the deployment platform. However, what if one cannot easily outfit their platform to record these demonstration signals or—worse yet—the demonstrator does not have access to the platform at all? Is imitation learning for vision-based autonomous navigation even possible in such scenarios?

arxiv-2304-08955.description: Abstract Abstract : We study the local-in-time well-posedness for an interface that separates an anisotropic plasma from a vacuum. The vacuum magnetic and electric fields are supposed to satisfy the pre-Maxwell equations.

arxiv-2306-05510.title: Uncovering Hidden Massive Black Hole Companions with Tidal Disruption Events astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 )
arxiv-2306-05510.creator: Brenna Mockler, Denyz Melchor, Smadar Naoz, Enrico Ramirez-Ruiz
arxiv-2306-05510.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Brenna Mockler, Denyz Melchor, Smadar Naoz, Enrico Ramirez-Ruiz. Dynamical perturbations from supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries can increase the rates of tidal disruption events (TDEs). However, most previous work focuses on TDEs from the heavier black hole in the SMBH binary (SMBHB) system. In this work, we focus on the lighter black holes in SMBHB systems and show that they can experience a similarly dramatic increase in their TDE rate due to perturbations from a more massive companion.

arxiv-2501-17879.creator: Sagnik Bhattacharya, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Ahsan Bilal, John M. Cioffi
arxiv-2501-17879.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sagnik Bhattacharya, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Ahsan Bilal, John M. Cioffi. Emerging wireless AR/VR applications require real-time transmission of correlated high-fidelity speech from multiple resource-constrained devices over unreliable, bandwidth-limited channels. Existing autoencoder-based speech source coding methods fail to address the combination of the following - (1) dynamic bitrate adaptation without retraining the model, (2) leveraging correlations among multiple speech sources, and (3) balancing downstream task loss with realism of reconstructed speech.
